drhp.business: The Company is engaged in the business of tea: it grows and manufactures Black Tea, including orthodox grades, through its Tea Division, whose named operating unit in this report is the Ananda Tea Estate. The industry-specific laws the secretarial auditor tests it against - the Tea Act, 1953, the Assam Tea Plantation Labour Act, 1951 and the Food Safety Standard Act, 2006 - describe a labour-intensive plantation operation, with 1477 permanent employees on the rolls as on 31.03.2026. risks.note: The MD&A names climate change as reducing both tea yield and quality, and says changes in weather pattern affect the timing of the tea flushes, making production less predictable - a direct hit to a single-crop plantation.
risks.risk: Climate change and shifting weather patterns

risks.note: The MD&A lists rising cost of wages, fertilizers, chemicals, power and fuel, transportation and packaging as a main challenge; with wages set under plantation labour law this is largely non-discretionary.
risks.risk: Cost inflation across the plantation cost base

risks.note: Labour shortages are named as an industry challenge; the Company runs a labour-intensive estate with 1477 permanent employees as on 31.03.2026 and is tested for compliance with the Assam Tea Plantation Labour Act, 1951.
risks.risk: Labour availability and plantation labour regulation

risks.note: Import competition is listed among the main challenges faced by the Indian tea industry, capping domestic price realisation.

The secretarial auditor records that 'The Company is engaged in the business of tea' and the notes carry the Textile business only as 'Since Discontinued', so earnings depend entirely on one crop at the Tea Division, whose only named unit is the Ananda Tea Estate.

Black Tea production moved down by about 14% in FY2025-26 while the result was carried by a 7.00% rise in average realisation; the North Eastern India average price itself rose about 11.23% off an unusually strong auction year, so a price reversal would not be cushioned by volume.

drhp.strategies: Modernise and augment the orthodox production facility - new rolling tables, balance shifters, sorting machines, colour sorter, dryer and ATM heater were installed during the year to cut cost and lift quality.|Stay a realisation-led producer: management frames the year's improvement in the Tea Division as coming from a 7.00% rise in average realisation rather than volume.|Maintain the estate's quality and sustainability accreditation (ISO 9001:2015, ISO 22000:2018, HACCP and the Trustea code for sustainable tea) as the basis for quality-linked pricing.
